Rotate a line 90 degrees on graph paper and track rise and run.

Goal: I can decide if lines are parallel, perpendicular, or neither from slopes or equations (used computationally here; proved in 9.10).

slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
The slope of a nonvertical line through (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is m = (y2 − y1)/(x2 − x1), rise over run.

Nonvertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal. Two lines, neither vertical, are perpendicular if and only if the product of their slopes is −1.

Rotating a slope triangle with run a and rise b by 90 degrees gives run −b and rise a, so slope b/a becomes −a/b, the negative reciprocal. We prove these criteria with similar triangles in 9.10.
